propositions: Enable verify.enforce_plan_material_pins and verify.require_plan_review_for_close in rebar.toml while library defaults remain false, with legacy unpinned attestations passing both gates.

End-to-end lifecycle tests prove that material changes trigger direct and transitive invalidation, unchanged re-reviews do not propagate, and depends_on/blocks references normalize to one canonical prerequisite.

Execution-phase plan edit, in-progress-to-open reset, code-only close freshness, enable/disable/re-enable cycles, and deleted/archived pinned target handling are demonstrated through public lifecycle surfaces.
No eager backfill, graph-wide invalidation event, new pin command, ordinary-list output change, or stored relation migration is introduced.

Real CLI invocation with no bypass proves four gate-health cases: legacy claim succeeds with exit 0, current-pinned close succeeds with exit 0, stale-pin-drift rejects with exit 1 and named tokens, and missing close-review rejects with exit 1 and remediation instruction.
Public lifecycle test suite passes with both policies enabled, and structured JSON evidence object with deterministic pass rule confirms all four fixture cases succeed.
